stories.headline: Update: Lawyers file habeas petition for Ecuadorian woman detained by ICE at Denver airport
stories.summary:
Attorneys at the Lichter Immigration law firm in Denver filed a federal habeas corpus petition Thursday on behalf of Chantal Alejandra Morales Rojas, 27, an Ecuadorian woman arrested by ICE agents at Denver International Airport on Monday while boarding a Southwest Airlines flight back to Oakland, Calif. The petition challenges her confinement at the immigration detention facility in Aurora. Video of her arrest at a DIA gate went viral on social media earlier this week.

Morales Rojas' attorneys say she entered the U.S. lawfully in January 2023 as a J-1 exchange visitor working as an au pair, and had a pending immigration application that authorized her to remain in the country and work while her case was under review. She had passed repeated background checks and had no criminal history, according to her legal team.

ICE previously stated that Morales Rojas entered the U.S. on Oct. 20, 2024, and overstayed her visa, which permitted her to stay only until Jan. 4, 2025. Her attorneys dispute that characterization, arguing the government was fully aware of her pending application and whereabouts for more than three years. The agency did not respond to a request for comment Friday.

stories.headline: Denver police arrest suspect in fatal North Columbine Street shooting
stories.summary:
Denver police announced Friday the arrest of Jacob Anglon, 29, in connection with a fatal Sunday morning shooting in the 1100 block of North Columbine Street. Anglon is suspected of shooting two men; one of the victims later died from his injuries. He was taken into custody Wednesday.

Anglon is being investigated for first-degree murder and attempted murder. The Denver District Attorney's Office will determine what formal charges to file. The Denver Office of the Medical Examiner has not yet publicly identified the victim.

The arrest adds to a series of violent incidents that have drawn police attention in Denver neighborhoods this summer. No further details about a motive or the circumstances of the shooting were immediately available.

stories.headline: Semitruck strikes pedestrian on I-25 near Loveland, man hospitalized with life-threatening injuries
stories.summary:
A semitruck struck a 66-year-old Berthoud man on southbound Interstate 25 near Loveland Friday morning after Colorado State Patrol received reports of a person running into traffic near U.S. 34. The pedestrian was transported to a hospital with life-threatening injuries. The truck driver was not injured and was not immediately charged or cited.

CSP said the initial report of a person running into traffic came in at approximately 8:45 a.m., with the crash occurring shortly thereafter. Southbound I-25 lanes were closed for an extended period before reopening at 4:29 p.m. The agency is continuing to investigate the incident.

Neither the pedestrian nor the driver was publicly identified in the CSP news release. The incident added to a string of serious crashes on Colorado's Front Range highways this summer.

stories.headline: Unaffiliated candidate Shimon Blau qualifies for ballot in Denver's 1st Congressional District
stories.summary:
Denver physician Shimon Blau has qualified as an unaffiliated candidate for the November ballot in Colorado's 1st Congressional District, setting up a long-shot challenge to Democrat Melat Kiros, who unseated longtime Rep. Diana DeGette in the primary. The Colorado Secretary of State's Office validated 1,918 of more than 2,200 signatures Blau submitted, surpassing the 1,500-signature threshold required to appear on the ballot.

Blau, a first-time candidate, said he entered the race due to concerns about Kiros' statements on Israel and her refusal to characterize last year's firebombing of a Jewish community rally in Boulder as antisemitic. He launched his signature-gathering campaign just days before the July 9 deadline.

The November ballot in the 1st District will also include Republican Christy Peterson, Libertarian Chad Humphrey, and Unity Party candidate Critter Milton. The district, which covers Denver, has long been a Democratic stronghold, making Kiros the heavy favorite in the general election.

stories.headline: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper to be arraigned Aug. 31 as legal case extends toward start of NFL season
stories.summary:
Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper appeared virtually Friday in a Douglas County courtroom and had his arraignment set for Aug. 31, a timeline that could push any potential trial into the start of the NFL regular season. Cooper, 28, faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, stemming from two arrests in June.

A forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend at Anschutz Medical Center in Aurora concluded she sustained strangulation with hypoxia and traumatic brain injury and faced a substantial risk of death, according to the district attorney's office. Cooper was first arrested June 4 following an incident at his Parker apartment, then arrested again June 12 on harassment and protection order violation charges.

The arraignment date creates a dilemma for the Broncos, who open the 2026 season Sept. 14 against the Chiefs in Kansas City. The NFL could place Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list if his trial extends into the season. Cooper has started 51 consecutive regular-season games and ranked second on the team with 8.0 sacks in 2025. Broncos head coach Sean Payton has said the club will follow league guidelines.

stories.headline: Bo Nix enters third Broncos season as polarizing quarterback with new offensive coordinator Davis Webb
stories.summary:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix heads into his third NFL season with a new offensive coordinator in Davis Webb, a simplified playbook and the addition of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle — developments the Denver Post's Troy Renck argues give Nix the best opportunity yet to prove his ceiling as a franchise quarterback. In two seasons, Nix has led Denver to a 24-win record, ended an eight-year playoff drought and captured the club's first AFC West title since Peyton Manning's final year.

Despite those results, Nix remains a divisional figure. Critics point to inconsistent play in the first three quarters of games, while supporters note his ability to limit turnovers and engineer late comebacks. CBS Sports recently labeled him one of the league's most overrated quarterbacks, while NFL players ranked him 59th in the Top 100, ahead of Lamar Jackson.

Coach Sean Payton acknowledged simplifying the offense after his lengthy play calls were seen as a contributing factor to offensive stagnation. Broncos players report to training camp July 28, with the first open practice July 31. The season opens Sept. 14 in Kansas City.

stories.headline: Colorado Avalanche sign forward Georgii Merkulov to one-year deal for 2026-27 season
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche have agreed to terms on a one-year, two-way contract with AHL veteran forward Georgii Merkulov for the 2026-27 season, the team announced. The two-way structure means Merkulov will earn different salaries depending on whether he plays in the NHL or AHL.

Merkulov has spent most of his professional career in the American Hockey League and gives the Avalanche additional forward depth as they continue to rebuild their roster. The signing comes amid an offseason in which Colorado has been active in adding lower-cost depth pieces.

The Avalanche have been relying increasingly on AHL talent to fill out their roster after trading away first-round picks in several recent NHL Drafts. Colorado's 2024 draft decision has drawn particular scrutiny given how those prospects have developed.

stories.headline: Denver gas prices climb back above $4 per gallon, driven by Iran conflict and global refining constraints
stories.summary:
The average price of gasoline in the Denver metro area rose to $4.11 per gallon Friday, up 15 cents over the past week and 37 cents higher than a month ago, according to GasBuddy data from 844 local stations. It marks the second time Denver prices have exceeded $4 since the start of the conflict in Iran.

GasBuddy petroleum analyst Patrick De Haan attributed the increase to three factors: the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, strained global refining capacity — worsened by continued Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries — and an upswing in local price cycling driven by higher crude oil costs. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, further tightening supply.

Nationally, the average gallon cost $4.01 on Friday, up about 11 cents in a week and 20 cents over a month. De Haan warned that motorists should brace for a rougher stretch ahead as market conditions are unlikely to ease in the near term.

stories.headline: Denver metro faces potential record high temperatures this weekend, heat advisories in effect
stories.summary:
The Denver metro area is bracing for a dangerous heat event this weekend, with forecast highs approaching 100 degrees Saturday and active Pinpoint Weather Alert Days issued for multiple counties, including Denver, north Douglas County, west Adams and Arapahoe counties, and east Broomfield County. Record high temperatures are possible across the metro and much of northeast Colorado.

Friday's high hovered in the mid-90s, with southerly winds around 10 miles per hour. The National Weather Service said the brief cooling brought by recent monsoon moisture has given way to another heat surge. The extreme heat follows a prolonged period of high temperatures across the region.

Residents are advised to limit outdoor exposure during peak afternoon hours, stay hydrated and check on vulnerable neighbors, particularly the elderly and those without access to air conditioning. The heat advisory covers a large swath of the Front Range.

stories.headline: Colorado Day 150 celebrations set for Aug. 1 across Denver metro with free events at Union Station, History Colorado
stories.summary:
Colorado marks its 150th birthday on Aug. 1, 2026, with a slate of free and low-cost events across the Denver metro. Denver Union Station will host a Colorado Day celebration from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. featuring gold panning, dummy steer roping, live music and historic walking tours, while History Colorado Center will offer free museum admission, a pancake breakfast and a sing-along with Isaac Slade of The Fray.

Stranahan's Whiskey Distillery in Denver is holding a river cleanup with the Greenway Foundation starting at 8 a.m., followed by distillery tours and a bottle launch for a Bottled-in-Bond American Single Malt Whiskey. The National Western Center will host the Mile Long Table community dinner at 5 p.m., with general admission starting at $5.28.

Events are also planned in Fort Collins, Pueblo and communities statewide. The sesquicentennial marks Colorado's admission to the Union on Aug. 1, 1876, earning it the nickname the Centennial State.

stories.headline: Denver Gazette editorial questions whether Polis competitiveness council is too little, too late for Colorado's business climate
stories.summary:
The Denver Gazette editorial board published a sharp critique Friday of Gov. Jared Polis' newly formed Governor's Competitiveness Council, arguing that the initiative — launched in the final months of a term-limited governor's tenure — is unlikely to reverse Colorado's deteriorating business rankings. Colorado dropped 14 spots on CNBC's "America's Top States for Business" list this year, falling from No. 11 to No. 25 in the largest single-year decline in the state's history on that index.

The editorial cited a letter from U.S. Rep. Gabe Evans to Polis outlining specific legislation the governor signed that Evans argued has harmed small businesses, including taxes on overtime pay, fees on diesel fuel and delivery services, and a 10-cent plastic bag fee. The board acknowledged Polis occasionally pushed back against his party's most business-unfriendly measures but said he ultimately presided over eight years of increasing regulatory burden.

Polis' office said the council will bring together public and private sector leaders to analyze the business landscape and develop a shared vision for Colorado's economic future, working in partnership with the Economic Development Council of Colorado. Critics argue that without the governor remaining in office to implement any resulting recommendations, the effort will have limited practical effect.

stories.headline: Things to do in metro Denver as July closes with fairs and festivals across the region
stories.summary:
The final week of July offers a range of community events across the Denver metro and broader Colorado, including fairs and festivals in Aurora, Castle Rock, Greeley, Conifer, Trinidad and Eagle, among other communities. The events span outdoor markets, county fairs and local celebrations as the summer season approaches its final stretch.

The activity calendar comes as Colorado Day preparations ramp up statewide, with August 1 sesquicentennial events anchoring a busy weekend for families and visitors. Denver venues and surrounding communities are hosting a mix of free and ticketed programming throughout the weekend.

Residents planning to attend outdoor events this weekend should be aware of the extreme heat forecast, with temperatures approaching 100 degrees Saturday across the metro. Organizers of outdoor events are encouraged to provide water stations and shade, and attendees are advised to take precautions.
